title: Simulated failure-driven promotion pipeline: shadow validation -> canary -> automated rollback simulation
creator: Avery Kim
description: Build a deployment pipeline that uses shadow traffic validation and a simulated-failure preflight to safely promote model variants from mirror validation into canary exposure and then to full traffic. The pipeline must respect environment-specific constraints (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC), compute a promotion confidence score from synthetic and live shadow comparisons, and run an automated rollback impact simulation before committing canary percentage changes in environments where capacity or isolation constraints exist.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can receive a new model variant and configure a shadow mirror against the active model for at least 1 hour using live traffic samples

Compute a promotion confidence score that combines (A) metric drift on key signals (latency, error-rate, semantic regression rate) between shadow and baseline and (B) synthetic test-suite pass rate; score is normalized 0..100

Pre-promotion rollback simulation runs in <30s and estimates the rollback impact on request routing and capacity for Dedicated and Private deployments (accounts for reserved GPU pools and tenant quotas)

When confidence >= configurable threshold (default 85) and preflight rollback simulation passes policy checks, orchestrator schedules canary growth steps per environment policy and emits a canary plan to the Console
Auto-rollback triggers if canary metrics breach configured SLO delta (latency P95 increase > 20% or error rate > 0.5% absolute) within the auto-rollback window
Deployment metadata, promotion decision, and rollback simulation outputs are recorded in audit logs and surfaced in Console UI and tracing
E2E tests for hosted/dedicated/private pipeline paths are added to CI with synthetic traffic replay harness
implementation_notes: Core components: (1) Shadow validator service that collects paired baseline/variant outputs and computes semantic regression via tokenizer-agnostic diff metrics; (2) Promotion confidence scorer combining live drift + synthetic evals; (3) Rollback impact simulator that replays the topology change against a capacity model (considers dedicated GPU reservations and network egress policy for private deployments); (4) Environment policy composer that enforces per-mode constraints (e.g., private can't exceed tenant-reserved capacity; hosted must respect global burst limits). The orchestrator should expose a single operator API: POST /orchestrate/promote with a policy payload and dry_run flag that returns confidence, simulated rollback consequence and a step-by-step canary plan.

Add environment policy composer with override rules for Private/VPC
